html:
The Dirty War was the campaign of state terror waged by the military dictatorship of Argentina, which seized power on 24 March 1976 and ruled until December 1983. Human rights groups estimate that up to 30,000 people were disappeared.

After the death of Perón, left-wing guerrillas and right-wing death squads fought, and the economy was in chaos. The junta of General Jorge Videla took power and set out to destroy the left. Security forces kidnapped students, unionists and activists, held them in secret camps such as the Navy Mechanics School, tortured them and killed most. Many were drugged and thrown from planes into the sea. Babies born to prisoners were given to military families.

The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo protested from 1977. After the Falklands War the junta fell. The report Nunca Más and the Trial of the Juntas in 1985 made Argentina a pioneer of justice after dictatorship. The regime took part in Operation Condor.
sum: The Dirty War was the campaign of state terror waged by the military dictatorship of Argentina, which seized power on 24 March 1976 and ruled until December 1983. Human rights groups estimate that up to 30,000 people were disappeared.
